outputs.exact_statement: For every odd positive integer $N$, every irreducible component of $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}T_2(N)$ has dimension exactly $4$.
The ring $A$ is compact, Hausdorff, and reduced. Its classical points are Zariski dense, and the operators $T_\ell,\ell S_\ell$, $\ell\nmid2N$, topologically generate it over $\mathbb Z_2$.

There is a continuous two-dimensional determinant over $A$ whose trace and determinant satisfy $$t(\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}_\ell)=T_\ell,\qquad
 d(\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}_\ell)=\ell S_\ell\qquad(\ell\nmid2N).$$
The ring $A$ is a finite product of complete Noetherian local rings with finite residue fields. Its given topology on each factor is the maximal-ideal-adic topology.
For the algebra $A$ in [eq:algebra], every irreducible component of $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}A$ has dimension at least $4$.
The closure of the classical points of bounded weight has dimension at most $1$. The closure of all Eisenstein points has dimension at most $2$.

For every minimal prime $P$ of $A$, there is a classical cuspidal map $\lambda:A\to\mathcal O_E$ of weight at least $3$ such that $P\subseteq\mathfrak x:=\ker\lambda$ and $\mathfrak x$ belongs to no other irreducible component of $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}A$.
For the representation [eq:r], $H^1_f(\mathbb Q,\mathop{\mathrm{ad}}r)=0$.
For every finite place $v$, $H^0(\mathbb Q_v,V^*(1))=0$, where $V=\mathop{\mathrm{ad}}r$.
For the representation $r$ of a cuspidal newform of weight at least $3$ and odd level dividing $N$, $$\dim_E H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,S},\mathop{\mathrm{ad}}r)\leq3.$$
